violations.description: Unsafe checkout of pull request code in pull_request_target workflow
violations.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/prt-dangerous-checkout.yml (line 19) checks out the attacker-controlled head ref in a `pull_request_target` context, which has access to repository secrets.
violations.recommendation: Avoid checking out the head ref of a PR in `pull_request_target` workflows; if necessary, do so without exposing secrets or running untrusted code.

violations.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/write-all-permissions.yml (line 12) uses `permissions: write-all`, which is risky, especially when combined with a `pull_request_target` trigger.
violations.recommendation: Explicitly define minimum required permissions for the workflow or individual jobs.

violations.description: Shell injection via untrusted GitHub Action expressions
violations.evidence: Untrusted event data is interpolated directly into shell scripts in .github/workflows/issue-labeler.yml (line 18: github.event.issue.title), .github/workflows/pr-comment-handler.yml (line 16), and .github/workflows/pr-title-injection.yml (lines 17-19).
violations.recommendation: Pass untrusted values to shell scripts using environment variables instead of direct interpolation.

violations.evidence: The project uses npm in its workflows (e.g., .github/workflows/no-permissions-declared.yml) but does not commit a package-lock.json file.
violations.recommendation: Generate and commit a package-lock.json file to ensure consistent builds.

violations.description: Missing permissions block in workflows triggered by untrusted events
violations.evidence: Workflows triggered by issues, issue_comment, or pull_request_target lack an explicit `permissions:` block, defaulting to broad access. Affected: .github/workflows/issue-labeler.yml, .github/workflows/pr-comment-handler.yml, .github/workflows/prt-dangerous-checkout.yml.
violations.recommendation: Add a top-level `permissions: {}` block to all workflows and grant only the specific scopes needed for each job.

violations.description: CI build steps will fail due to missing manifest files
violations.evidence: The workflows .github/workflows/no-permissions-declared.yml (line 25) and .github/workflows/prt-dangerous-checkout.yml (line 25) call `npm ci` and `npm test`, but the project lacks a package.json file.
violations.recommendation: Add a package.json and package-lock.json to the repository to allow CI to install dependencies and run tests.

violations.description: CI runs tests that do not exist
violations.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/no-permissions-declared.yml (line 26) runs `npm test`, but there are no tests or package.json defined in the repository.
violations.recommendation: Add tests and a package.json manifest, or remove the test execution from CI.

violations.description: Automated merging of pull requests without review
violations.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/write-all-permissions.yml (line 21) uses `gh pr merge --auto` to merge pull requests without a manual approval gate.
violations.recommendation: Implement a manual review process or require status checks and approvals before merging.

violations.evidence: The repository does not contain a .gitignore file to prevent tracking of temporary or generated files.
violations.recommendation: Add a .gitignore file appropriate for a Node.js project.

violations.evidence: The repository has no configuration for linting or formatting tools (e.g., ESLint, Prettier), which are standard for Node.js projects.
violations.recommendation: Configure a linter (like ESLint) and a formatter (like Prettier) to ensure code consistency and catch potential issues.
